source_text: Deng Xiaoping was the paramount leader of the reform era, and few doubted it.

source_text: historians of the soviet period have long debated whether the reforms of the late nineteen seventies changed the fundamental character of the political system or merely adjusted its outer forms while leaving the inner core of one party rule untouched and whether the new institutions that emerged from the transition represented a genuine break with the authoritarian past or a more efficient way of preserving the same hierarchy of power under a new set of labels and a younger generation of leaders who had grown up inside the old apparatus and learned its habits of command and caution and secrecy so the scholarly argument turned again and again on the question of continuity and change and on the evidence that could be drawn from the archives of the party and the state and from the memoirs of the officials who had served at the highest levels of the old order
